newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee mildly up vs forward dlr, spot steady.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee mildly up vs forward dlr, spot steady.

text.p: The Indian rupee was mildly up against the forward dollar on Tuesday, largely reflecting easing call money rates, dealers said.
"There is some receiving (of premiums for forward dollar sale), but only for the near term," said a dealer.
August dollars were quoted at 7/9 paise in latest quotes compared with 8/10 paise opening, dealers said. September dollars eased to 17/19 paise from 18/20 paise opening.
Overnight call rates eased to 3.25/3.50 percent from 3.75/4.75 percent opening, dealers said.
The spot dollar was steady at 35.702/705 in latest quotes.

"People are taking RBI intervention for granted," said a dealer at a foreign bank, referring to Reserve Bank of India's intervention on Monday morning. Its dollar purchases propped up the dollar to 35.70 level from 35.69 rupees.
The RBI has been intervening throughout last week to arrest the rupee's rise above the 35.70-mark.
